substantiveDecisions.reason: The NCBE primary AMG page identifies Aspergillus niger glucoamylase acting on alpha-1,4 and alpha-1,6 links to release glucose from liquefied starch. The liquid AMG300L product is identified rather than an arbitrary amylase. pH4.50 and60°C/60min are an explicit adapted teaching condition, not asserted optimum or quantitative conversion. Record actual identity/lot/activity, pH and temperature; trade-name activity establishes no application yield.

Potato-starch gelatinisation precedes enzyme addition; all corresponding matrices get the same initial heat history. NCBE states AMG survives60°C for an hour and requires about80°C for denaturation; the defined80–85°C/10min control is reasonable but honestly not claimed to have zero residual enzyme. H/I/N compare active enzyme, heat-treated enzyme and no enzyme. E/EI explicitly address reducing sugars in the supplied liquid carrier; simple blank subtraction is not treated as a complete material balance.

1.9212g anhydrous citric acid is0.0100mol and filling to1.000L gives10mmol/L total citrate. Measured pH4.50 after adjustment/filling remains controlling. Each batch has100.0mL aqueous liquid before yeast:99+1 for enzyme conditions or100 for N/G;10g substrate where listed and1.00g yeast where listed. Withdrawn suspension liquid is quantitatively returned. Mass replacement is limited to plausible evaporation, not spilled substrate.

All preparations cool to30±1°C before yeast, and active/inactive/no-yeast controls separate biological activity. Twenty minutes and actual0/5/10/15/20 readings are specified. A freely moving syringe/free gas path,80mL stop and honest interrupted-run records prevent treating a blocked/censored run as a full20-minute measurement. Neither complete hydrolysis nor a specified gas result is promised. Comparisons must respect actual matched times and disturbed controls.

The method explicitly requires actual filtration, recorded filtrate volume/losses/appearance and personal action observations. Particles/cells may be retained while dissolved sugars and possible fermentation products pass. It claims no pure ethanol, selective dissolved-product separation, tasting or food use. Gas alone identifies neither CO2 nor ethanol/glucose; carrier sugars prevent a standalone Benedict result from identifying starch-derived glucose.
